speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, technology has increasingly enabled scammers to operate at scale across the globe and their tactics have become more sophisticated by the year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Yet, while the tactics have changed, at its heart, scammers use the tried-and-tested formula of exploiting their victims’ fears and hopes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers do not respect geographical boundaries, seeking out victims wherever they can.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong has spoken about the enhanced protections in our banking system.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will focus on the upstream measures – how we can intervene through our communications infrastructure to fight scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This addresses questions by Mr Alex Yam regarding CSA’s assessment and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim on whether financial institutions met cybersecurity standards.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If I could use an analogy in the physical world, the scammers in this case did not manufacture a special key or special keys to break into the bank premises and to steal from the customers’ deposit boxes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, they stood in front of the bank and tricked customers into handing over their identity cards (IC) and keys.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They then pretended to the bank teller that they were the real customers, accessed the deposit boxes and cleared them out quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Because the scammer looked real by wearing the correct uniform and name tag bearing the bank’s logo.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Because the scammer was in possession of items that only real customers were expected to have.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the physical world, the scammer’s pressure tactics to hand over the IC and key might have raised an alarm.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Likewise, for the bank, branch managers might have noticed and made gentle enquiries as to the hurried manner in which the deposit boxes were emptied out.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But in the digital world, where we have become so used to instant communications and transactions, our guard is down.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The use of SMS to reach potential victims is, unfortunately, becoming even more common and sophisticated.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers have used it together with phone calls and emails to phish for information or spoof legitimate organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, scammers are taking advantage of our communications infrastructure to reach even more potential victims, faster.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To combat phishing and spoofing by scammers, we should disrupt as many parts of their modus operandi as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Apart from enhanced safeguards in the banking system to prevent scams from easily succeeding, upstream measures are also needed to disrupt scammers’ reach to potential victims.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Christopher de Souza are, therefore, right to ask how we can strengthen our defences through our telco networks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is useful to first step through how a phishing and spoofing scam is usually carried out.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Typically, the scammer starts by contacting the victim, through phone calls or SMS.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The victim is then tricked into surrendering their credentials or personal information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In many cases, the act of surrendering credentials and personal information takes place on a scam website, something designed to look like the real website of a legitimate organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Compared to asking for such information by phone or SMS, no direct human interactions are required since victims themselves enter their details on a scam website.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This allows such scams to be processed with greater scale and speed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And this is why much of our upstream measures have focused on blocking scam websites.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is a key part of disrupting the scammers’ plans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On any given day, more than 90% of Singaporeans go online for various activities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SPF and IMDA work closely with Internet Service Providers to block scam websites.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When consumers are led by scammers to these websites, they will be alerted to be vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Countless more victims would have been otherwise scammed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, we have the capacity to block many more suspicious websites.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, this does not mean that they will completely disappear from our screens.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because scammers react quickly and dynamically to such blocks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the peak, we blocked around 52 sites in a single day or one every 30 minutes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the scammers were quick to create new websites over the course of their campaign.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to strengthen detection and reporting mechanisms to be more responsive.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As mentioned by Minister Wong earlier, the banks will be enhancing their fraud surveillance systems.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Government agencies will also explore the use of artificial intelligence to more quickly identify and block scam websites.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, the National Crime Prevention Council will start a WhatsApp channel to crowdsource from the public, information on scam websites and messages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To ensure processes are in place for proper follow-up, this channel will be launched by the third quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Website blocking is part of the suite of upstream measures to disrupt the scammers’ plans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But before they are lured to a scam website, victims may have been contacted by phone or SMS.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sometimes, the scammers get what they want without even leading the victim to a scam website.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members will be familiar with scam callers impersonating officials from China.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: During COVID-19 times, the scam callers switched their masquerades, pretending to be the Police or other trusted organisations, such as MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their messages were adapted to exploit concerns about vaccination or other COVID-19-related measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These calls deploy what is known as "social engineering" techniques to cause fear and panic in their victims, using topical concerns that scammers know people are worried about.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As most of these calls come from overseas, scammers will often seek to appear more credible by spoofing local numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: An important set of upstream measures, therefore, involves blocking these suspicious calls.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We expect the number of scam calls to rise, given the changing tactics of scammers to increase their reach.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They include, for example, incoming overseas calls that resemble phone numbers of our local Government agencies or emergency services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overseas scam callers may also add a prefix "65", without the "+" prefix, to give the impression that they are calling from within Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many scam calls were averted through such measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about the Do Not Call (DNC) registry.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The DNC registry was not designed to prevent scam messages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, it was created to allow individuals to opt out of receiving unsolicited telemarketing messages or calls.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers will, of course, not take the trouble to check this registry before conducting their illegal activities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even if our telcos can block millions of incoming overseas calls, we must not be lulled into a false sense of security.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Moreover, as each avenue becomes harder to break through, scammers turn to other channels.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the case of the OCBC scams, the SMS channel was exploited.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To better understand how it happened, it is useful, firstly, to recognise that SMS is an old technology.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For many Singaporeans, it is more common these days to communicate with each other using messaging platforms, such as WhatsApp and Telegram.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nevertheless, SMS is still being used by many organisations because it is a cheap and convenient way to reach many customers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All handphones, whether smart or not, can receive SMS.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the SMS system was never designed for secure communications.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Together with its widespread use, this makes it an attractive channel for scammers to reach potential victims.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, legitimate senders can use an alphanumeric ID to make themselves more easily known to customers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead of a string of numbers, customers receive an SMS from a sender identified as, say, "ABC company".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, this alphanumeric ID is not automatically protected as part of the SMS protocol.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means, unfortunately, that a scammer can use the same alphanumeric ID "ABC Company" and enter the message thread between the legitimate business sender and its customer.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members know by now this was what happened in the OCBC scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result, the victims did not even realise they were communicating with the scammer, rather than OCBC itself.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Melvin Yong asked how SMS could be made safer.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The gap I described above had, in fact, been identified by MAS and IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, the agencies started a pilot for SMS Sender ID protection.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: An organisation can register the alphanumeric ID that they use, thus reducing the risk of an illegitimate sender spoofing the same alphanumeric ID and having the message appear within the same message thread.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SMSes that try to spoof registered IDs will thus not be delivered, as the sender details would not match registry records.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All organisations seeking to send SMSes using registered IDs to phone subscribers in Singapore must also have a valid Unique Enterprise Number (UEN).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will help Police with investigations in the event of a scam.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Once these immediate measures are completed, the threat surface will be reduced.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, if an alphanumeric ID is not placed by an organisation into the registry, it cannot be protected.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Observers have also pointed out that scammers can still use similar-looking alphanumeric IDs that are not in the registry, to trick potential victims.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To further close these gaps, we will consider requiring all users of alphanumeric IDs to be registered.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers will then not be able to send SMS using alphanumeric IDs except by joining the registry.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will also provide more assurance to receivers of SMS messages that an alphanumeric ID indicates a registered source.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These further measures will take time to implement and come at a cost, including to businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their customers can then choose to save the number in their own contact list to help them recognise future messages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, organisations should rethink how they use SMS to communicate with their customers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As I have mentioned earlier, SMS was never meant for secure communications.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Where the message contains or will lead to the transmission of sensitive, confidential information or high value transactions, there should be more restraint.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are generally safe, but we would not send very valuable items even using registered post.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One other area that Dr Shahira Abdullah asked about was clickable links.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although her question was related to its use by MOH, the considerations are applicable to many other agencies and companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members will know that clickable links are everywhere.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They appear on websites, in our emails and, of course, our SMS messages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: You find them, too, in WhatsApp, Telegram and many other apps.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are used extensively because they are highly effective in getting people to take action.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, using such links, millions of vaccination appointments were quickly and conveniently booked.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Unfortunately, clickable links have also been used for criminal purposes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, the removal of clickable links in many other settings will only erode convenience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More importantly, the loss of effective outreach in cases like vaccination registration could be detrimental to our people.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A blanket removal must, therefore, be very carefully considered.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, some Members asked if the OCBC scam was a result of a cyber attack, or a breach of the bank's IT system which had enabled the criminals to carry out their crimes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What they did were classic acts of deception by misleading the victims into believing that they were communicating with the bank and, therefore, tricking the victims into providing their account details.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With these stolen account details, scammers then logged into the victims’ bank accounts and stole the victims’ hard-earned monies via electronic transfers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Once again, the communication system has become the channel for scammers to get into contact with victims at scale and quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, compared to the past, the scammers’ acts of deception were far more realistic this time.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Meanwhile, IMDA has enhanced preventive measures in the communication infrastructure, and MHA has also strengthened public education efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In combination, these multi-layered measures are aimed at disrupting scam syndicates' modus operandi.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, we all know that every move that we make to derail the syndicates will be countered by more sophisticated moves by them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When carrying out their crimes, the scammers have no regard for borders nor the law; whenever we come up with new countermeasures, they will certainly also be cooking up new ways to continue with their operations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even with new measures in place, everyone in the ecosystem must work together and raise our defences in all areas to prevent these criminals from succeeding easily.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, our additional safeguards underscore the importance of telcos in combating phishing and spoofing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also expect them to do more to help their customers avoid becoming victims.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Scammers change methods and tactics to evade detection and our capabilities will need to, likewise, adapt.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA will work with the telcos to continuously strengthen their anti-scam capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We should recognise that, even with best efforts, the network defences alone cannot block all scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At every part of the chain, upstream and downstream, we are taking steps to reduce the risk.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The measures in our communications infrastructure, for example, reduce the available avenues for scammers to reach victims.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As mentioned by Minister Lawrence Wong, MCI is also working with MAS to consider the shared responsibilities of all the key stakeholders in the ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Taken together, we should be able to significantly reduce the risk of consumers falling victim to scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Indeed, I would add that our approach is an ecosystem approach — what was described by Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This has multiple layers of defence – no single layer providing a complete answer, but all layers reinforcing each other to disrupt the scammers' plans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Mr Sitoh Yih Pin's question, this will prevent some types of scams from recurring.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But our best defence against new types of scams is a vigilant public.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ultimately, they determine the extent to which we can prevent scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The public should, therefore, also arm themselves with knowledge on scams and how to protect themselves and their loved ones who might be less tech-savvy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are tools, such as ScamShield, that can help to prevent some scam calls and SMSes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Minister of State Desmond Tan will say more on these later.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, for our own long-term success as a nation, digital transformation must continue.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Alex Yam is rightly concerned about the impact of these scams on digital adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will strengthen public confidence in online transactions, raise awareness on good cyber-hygiene habits and bolster the digital resilience of our citizens, a call also made by Miss Cheng Li Hui.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is part of a whole-of-nation approach to safeguard Singaporeans against online threats, especially for the more vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many partners have kickstarted projects related to digital literacy and wellness.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The DfL Movement will do its part to complement efforts by SPF, the National Crime Prevention Council and CSA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These are available and translated into the vernacular languages for different audiences.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All of us – banking institutions, telco operators, Government, businesses, individuals – have a role to play in the fight against scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But they are necessary to better safeguard our people from scams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Equally importantly, they will help to uphold confidence in our digital journey.
